title: EPT (Extended Page Table) entry
summary: An EPT entry is 8 bytes (64 bits), similar to a regular page table entry but for guest physical → host physical translation. Fields: read (bit 0), write (bit 1), execute (bit 2), memory type (bits 3-5), ignore PAT (bit 6), accessed (bit 8), dirty (bit 9), execute for user (bit 10), reserved (bit 11), host physical frame (bits 12-51), reserved (bits 52-60), suppress VE (bit 61), reserved (bits 62-63).

ext.summary: An EPT entry is 8 bytes (64 bits), similar to a regular page table entry but for guest physical → host physical translation. Fields: read (bit 0), write (bit 1), execute (bit 2), memory type (bits 3-5), ignore PAT (bit 6), accessed (bit 8), dirty (bit 9), execute for user (bit 10), reserved (bit 11), host physical frame (bits 12-51), reserved (bits 52-60), suppress VE (bit 61), reserved (bits 62-63).

structure.meaning: 000 = uncacheable, 001 = write combining, 010 = write through, 011 = write back, 100 = write protected, 101 = write back (UC if MTRR says UC).

notes: EPT provides nested paging: guest virtual → guest physical → host physical.
EPT violations cause VM exits (or #VE if enabled).
EPT is used by KVM, Hyper-V, VMware for memory virtualization.
EPT adds one more level of translation (guest virtual → guest physical → host physical).
Without EPT, shadow page tables are used (software-based, slower).
